messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Status] US-East hosted API: Increased latency & partial degradation (GreenBridge Health)

Hi Sarah and team,

We want to make you aware of a current issue affecting our hosted API endpoints in the us-east region that may impact GreenBridge Health integrations. Symptoms we are seeing: elevated tail latency for generation requests (notably >95th pct), intermittent 502s for some short-lived sessions, and delayed batch completions.

Impact: a subset of requests routed to our standard pooled capacity may experience latency spikes or transient failures. Requests routed to Dedicated/Reserved pools are not impacted.

What we're doing: engineering has opened an incident bridge and is actively rolling back a configuration change to the autoscaling/routing policy that appears correlated with the spike. We're also enabling a temporary fallback routing rule to send traffic to reserved nodes for higher-priority tenants.

Immediate mitigations:
- Fallback routing enabled (best-effort) to reserved capacity for interactive requests
- Increased monitoring granularity and alerting on 5xx/latency

Next update: 30 minutes or sooner if we have a material change.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-07-22-us-east-latency (live)

Attachments: incident-snapshot.png (png) — current p90/p95 graphs

We understand the disruption this can cause and will prioritize updates for you. If you need us to fail requests to your private dedicated pool or pause non-critical jobs, let me know and I can coordinate immediately.

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Principal Incident Manager, Redwood Inference

Diego / Ben — quick internal note to align before the next customer update.

Observations from the bridge: the spike started after a config push to the pooled autoscaler at ~08:50 PDT. The change altered the cooldown/scale-in thresholds; under certain request distributions the pooled nodes compact and increase KV cache misses, causing higher latency and a flurry of upstream 502s.

Current plan:
- Rollback the autoscaler change (in progress) — target completion in ~20–25 minutes
- Activate additional prefix KV caching for high-throughput models (short term patch)
- Route high-priority interactive traffic to reserved capacity (done as of 09:25, partially effective)

Customer comms: recommend telling customers (1) why this happened at a high level, (2) what we did (rollback + fallback), and (3) when we'll send a postmortem. Also let's proactively offer a credit if GreenBridge shows SLA breach. Ben, can you confirm the credit policy?

— Marissa

Subject: [Update] US-East hosted API: Fallback routing active, latency improving

Hi Sarah — quick update following our internal changes.

What changed: we rolled back the autoscaler configuration and activated the fallback routing to reserved nodes for interactive/generation requests. Early signals are positive: median latency is back near baseline and p95 is trending down. Some long-running batch jobs are still experiencing delayed completion as they remain queued on pooled capacity.

Answers to your questions:
1) ETA: interactive traffic is expected to be back to normal within ~10–20 minutes for most customers; we will confirm when p95 stabilizes for GreenBridge.
2) Data/duplicates: there is no evidence of lost messages; a small number of failed requests were retried by clients. If you have idempotency keys for the affected timeframe (08:45–09:05 PDT), share them and we will run a targeted check.
3) Postmortem/credits: we will publish a postmortem within 72 hours and are prepared to offer a credit if SLA thresholds are breached. Ben, please follow up with finance for specifics.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-07-22-us-east-latency
Attachments: incident-graphs.png (png) — p50/p95/time-series since 08:30

I'll send another note when we mark the incident resolved, and once we have the postmortem draft.

Thanks for flagging the idempotency concern; we'll prioritize any targeted checks you send.

Diego

Subject: [Resolved] US-East hosted API: Incident resolved; postmortem & next steps

Hi Sarah — final update for the incident earlier today.

Status: Resolved at 15:00 PDT. Traffic has been stable for several hours and p95/p99 metrics are within normal ranges.

Root cause (summary): A configuration change to the pooled autoscaler changed scale-in thresholds under heavy short-burst traffic, producing compacted node pools with increased KV cache miss rates. This amplified tail latency and led to transient 502s for a subset of pooled requests.

Remediations completed:
- Rolled back autoscaler change to previous safe settings
- Activated fallback routing during the incident to reserve capacity for interactive traffic
- Implemented short-term KV cache guards to reduce miss amplification

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Full postmortem being drafted; we'll share within 72 hours (link and calendar invite to review).
- Engineering will add a canary gate for autoscaler changes and a pre-deploy traffic model to prevent similar regressions.
- We are ready to review idempotency keys you provide and will proactively run checks for duplicates.
- Support/Finance will follow up on SLA credits if GreenBridge meets breach conditions (Ben to own).

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx (docx) — early draft with timelines and remediation items
Related ticket: JIRA SUP-3891
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-07-22-us-east-latency

If you'd like a review call, we're available tomorrow afternoon; I'll send a calendar invite unless you prefer a different time. Thank you for your patience — we're sorry for the disruption and appreciate your partnership.

Best,
Diego
